'''Andrea Bréard''' (also published as Andrea Eberhard and Andrea Eberhard-Bréard) is a German [[history of mathematics|historian of mathematics]] and [[sinology|sinologist]] specializing in [[Chinese mathematics]]. She is [[Alexander von Humboldt Professorship|Alexander von Humboldt Professor]] of Sinology in the Department of Classical World and Asian Cultures at the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg]].{{r|humboldt}}

==Education and career==
Bréard earned a diploma in mathematics at the [[Technical University of Munich]] in 1991. After continuing study in China at [[Fudan University]],{{r|fau}} she returned to Germany for a PhD at [[Technische Universität Berlin]] in 1997, supervised by [[Eberhard Knobloch]].{{r|mg}} She earned a second doctorate in 1998 in France through [[Paris Diderot University]],{{r|fau}} and completed a [[habilitation]] at Technische Universität Berlin in 2008.{{r|fau}}

She worked as a researcher at the [[Technical University of Munich]] from 1992 to 2004, under the direction of {{ill|Konrad Königsberger|de}}. From 2005 to 2017 she was [[maître de conférences]] at the [[University of Lille]] in France, also holding various short-term positions in France, Germany, and the US. From 2017 to 2021 she held a professorship at [[Paris-Saclay University]],{{r|fau}} and in 2021 she moved to the University of Erlangen–Nuremberg as Humboldt Professor.{{r|humboldt}}

==Recognition==
Bréard was one of two 1998 recipients of the thesis prize of the Association française d'études chinoises.{{r|afec}} She was the 1999 recipient of the prize for young historians of the [[International Academy of the History of Science]].{{r|prix}}

Bréard was elected as a corresponding member of the International Academy of the History of Science in 2015.{{r|iahs}} She was elected to the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] in 2021.{{r|leo}}

==Books==
Bréard's books include:

*''Re-Kreation eines mathematischen Konzeptes im chinesischen Diskurs: "Reihen" vom 1. bis zum 19. Jahrhundert'' [''Re-creation of a mathematical concept in Chinese discourse: "Series" from the first to the nineteenth century''] (dissertation, TU Berlin, 1997; Boethius: Texte und Abhandlungen zur Geschichte der Mathematik und der Naturwissenschaften, vol. 42, Franz Steiner Verlag, 1999){{r|r1mk}}
*''Reform, Bureaucratic Expansion and Production of Numbers: Statistics in Early 20th Century China'' (Habilitationsschrift, TU Berlin, 2008)
*''Nine Chapters on Mathematical Modernity: Essays on the Global Historical Entanglements of the Science of Numbers in China'' (Transcultural Research—Heidelberg Studies on Asia and Europe in a Global Context, Springer, 2019){{r|9cmm}}
*''Li Shanlan. Catégories analogues d'accumulations discrètes.'' [''Analogical categories of discrete accumulations''] (Bibliothèque chinoise, vol. 40, Les Belles Lettres, 2023)
